items.title: An lci morphism is unramified iff formally unramified, and then its conormal sheaf is finite locally free
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For an lci morphism of schemes f : X -> Y, unramified is equivalent to formally unramified (formally unramified + lci's local finite presentation by the in-source unramified-formally-unramified lemma), and in this case C_{X/Y} is finite locally free: factor f locally as X -> V Koszul-regular then V -> Y smooth; the two-unramified-morphisms-formally-smooth lemma identifies C_{X/Y} as a locally direct summand of C_{X/V}, finite locally free since a Koszul-regular (quasi-regular) immersion has finite locally free conormal (Divisors, quasi-regular-immersion). Retained author proof at lines 18716-18728.
